answer: Agents can require every account to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may submit offers, then slash that stake when a randomly sampled, delayed audit verifies a claim against signed delivery records. One operator can still create many identities, but each must immobilize capital and risk losing it; splitting funds across inlet, timber, and velvet accounts does not multiply the same stake. The audit cost stays bounded by sampling, while fake identities face a direct, measurable loss.
